insight: The worker short-circuits all election logic after ELECTION_DAY (2026-03-03): runDailyUpdate and runCountyRefresh return { skipped: true } (no countyLog/countiesRefreshed/county fields), and the guide/summary/stream endpoints return 410 Gone. Any test asserting pre-election behavior MUST freeze the clock or it becomes a time bomb that goes red the day after the election. Use vi.useFakeTimers({ now: new Date('2026-02-20T12:00:00Z'), toFake: ['Date'] }) in beforeEach + vi.useRealTimers() in afterEach. CRITICAL: pass toFake:['Date'] when the code under test calls sleep()/setTimeout (e.g. runCountyRefresh sleeps 3-5s between counties) — faking setTimeout too makes those sleeps hang forever and the test times out. Date-only faking freezes the clock while leaving real timers intact. Phase can also be forced via KV (site_phase:tx) or ?test_phase= query param, which is preferable for tests specifically exercising post-election behavior.
evidence: 2026-05-26 — full CI suite had been red since the March 3 primary; 19 tests across 5 files failed with 'expected undefined to be defined' / 'expected 410 to be 400'. Fixed by freezing the clock per-block (commit abd7347). 2219/2219 tests green after.
